tldr: Headlines across 14 country-buckets converge on three claims: Israeli strikes are still killing Palestinians on the ceasefire anniversary, hunger and healthcare have not recovered, and the ceasefire's political promises remain mostly unmet. The security frame dominates, carried by 7 of 14 buckets — a harder, more alarm-oriented surface than the body-pass balance of policy and lived-experience angles.

silences.note: NPR's headline ('A year of ceasefire in Gaza through the lens of NPR's reporter') is meta-journalistic — it describes the act of witnessing rather than making a substantive claim about security, health, or policy, and fits no frame in the closed codebook.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to use 'sham' as a descriptor for the ceasefire directly in the headline — the most explicitly delegitimising language across all 25 titles.
Only outlet to label the ceasefire 'US-brokered' in its headline, foregrounding American sponsorship of an agreement that is visibly failing.
Places 'ceasefire' in scare quotes in both its headlines, signalling editorial rejection of the term; unique among wire and broadcast outlets in the corpus.

bottom_line: The headline layer of this corpus leads overwhelmingly with Israeli strikes still killing Palestinians on the ceasefire anniversary — a security-first surface that compresses the policy failure and humanitarian collapse the body pass develops at length into a single brutal fact: the killing has not stopped.
